summary: Retry flare exposes soft 429 queueing as perceived inference timeout for BrightWell Health
description:
Issue summary:
BrightWell Health reports intermittent long-tail inference requests that clients treat as timeouts. After retries the customer sees either 429s followed by cascading retries or multi-second queuing before a 200 response. Customer perceives an LLM regression (slower model) but behavior correlates with quota-window enforcement combined with aggressive client retry behavior.

Impact:
- Several user-facing endpoints in BrightWell reporting 5-12s p95 latency and spikes of 503/504s during peak minutes.
- Customer disabled feature flag for recommendations as a mitigation.
- Affects production (dedicated pool) in us-east for a subset of tenants.

Environment:
- Deployment: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool)
- Region: us-east primary, occasional occurrences in eu-west replica
- SDK: redwood-js v1.8.2 running server-side in customer app containers
- Model: redwood-v1-compat (pinned) for recommendation endpoint

Steps to reproduce (customer supplied):
1) Send 80 requests/sec with client concurrency 60 from a single service host using SDK default retry policy (exponential backoff, no jitter).
2) Observe some requests receive 429 soft-throttle signals with X-RateLimit-* headers indicating sliding window bursts.
3) Client retries immediately (backoff base small) which causes short retry bursts and visible queueing on the serving-runtime and scheduler, producing long-tail latency for otherwise healthy requests.

Logs & traces provided by customer:
- Example request-id: r-8f4a2c9b (timestamp 2026-03-10T15:23:12Z) - shows initial 429 then two rapid retries then a 200 at 15:23:21Z.
- SDK trace: retry attempts at +150ms, +400ms, +900ms (no jitter).
- Serving-runtime traces show short token-queue delay spikes aligned with retry bursts.

Immediate customer-facing workaround requested.
comments: 2026-03-10 15:38 - BrightWell Support Engineer (L. Chen): Customers see p95 spikes and are rolling back recommendation feature. Provided initial traces and asked for immediate mitigation options.

2026-03-10 16:05 - Support (A. Martinez): Logged ticket, requested request-ids and client SDK config. Suggested temporary mitigation: reduce client concurrency and add randomized jitter between retries; recommended parsing X-RateLimit headers and backing off on 429s.

2026-03-10 17:12 - SRE (R. Patel): Pulled serving-runtime traces for r-8f4a2c9b. Observed short-lived token queueing on scheduler during window boundary. No model-level regression found (latency inside model execution steady). Likely client retry bursts are synchronizing with sliding-window quota enforcement.

2026-03-11 09:30 - Customer (BrightWell): Applied suggested jitter and lowered concurrency from 60 to 10. Reported immediate improvement in tail latency. Still seeing occasional spikes during minute-boundary bursts (activity pattern aligned to cron job).

2026-03-11 11:00 - Support (A. Martinez): Recommended enabling client-side parsing of X-RateLimit-Reset and implement exponential backoff with full jitter. Suggested moving high-rate cron to staggered timing. Opened follow-up task with Runtime team to investigate smoothing at quota-service.

2026-03-12 10:50 - Runtime Eng (M. Gomez): Deployed rate-window smoothing patch to quota-service that staggers soft-throttle enforcement over a 10s ramp window (can be disabled per-customer). Applied to BrightWell's dedicated pool as trial. Monitoring shows reduced visible queueing spikes.
2026-03-12 12:20 - Customer (BrightWell): Confirmed p95 returned to baseline after both client-side changes and server-side smoothing. Customer requested guidance doc for SDK retry config.
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis: Per-minute sliding-window soft-throttle enforcement creates micro-bursts where many concurrent clients receive 429s and immediately retry with similar backoff schedules. These synchronized retry flares produce short-lived queueing at the scheduler and token cache contention, which looks like an inference regression to the customer. Evidence: request timelines, serving-runtime queue metrics correlated to retry spikes, model execution time metrics unchanged. Additional signal: cron-like workload at customer triggered synchronization.
Actions taken: reviewed request traces, repro with customer-supplied workload pattern in staging, validated that adding jitter/decreasing concurrency reduces tail. Implemented temporary smoothing in quota-service for BrightWell dedicated pool.
Next steps: create guidance doc for SDK best-practices, add server-side opt-in smoothing feature for other customers, evaluate making smoothing default for dedicated pools with bursty patterns.
resolution:
Workaround and fixes applied: 1) Customer implemented immediate mitigation by lowering client concurrency and switching to exponential backoff with full jitter; 2) Runtime team deployed quota-service smoothing for BrightWell's dedicated pool; 3) Support provided SDK retry configuration guidance and recommended staggering scheduled jobs.
Status: Customer confirmed baseline p95 restored. Follow-up items: create support KB article for "Handling 429s and retry jitter best practices" and add a backlog task to expose rate-limit headers in redwood-js telemetry. Planned owner for KB: Developer Experience (J. Ko).
